issues.description: The problem statement requires the subroutine set_pixel to preserve all registers except EAX ("Außer dem Register eax dürfen keine anderen Registerinhalte verändert werden"). The solution implementation of set_pixel (solution_repository/pixel.asm lines 19-37) uses and modifies EDI without saving/restoring it (instructions 'or edi, edi' and 'jz .skip_alpha' reference/modify EDI but there is no push/pop/restore for EDI). This violates the calling convention/contract specified in the problem and can change the caller's EDI unexpectedly, confusing students and breaking the stated requirement. The template provides an empty stub for set_pixel (template_repository/pixel.asm lines 36-38) so students would implement according to the spec; the provided solution therefore demonstrates an implementation that does not conform to the specification.
issues.suggested_fix:
Ensure the set_pixel implementation preserves all registers except EAX as required. Two safe approaches: (A) Do not use EDI at all — compute x*4 via a shift (shl) into a temporary register that is preserved (e.g., use ESI after pushing/popping it), compute y*7680 using an instruction that does not clobber EDX (or restore EDX), and write [address] from ECX. Or (B) if EDI must be used, explicitly save and restore it at function entry/exit (push edi ... pop edi) so the caller's EDI is unchanged. Also remove the unnecessary 'or edi, edi' / alpha-check code that references EDI unpredictably. Example fix (conceptual):

set_pixel:
    push ebx
    push esi
    push edi        ; save EDI if you use it

    mov esi, eax
    shl esi, 2      ; esi = x * 4
    mov eax, 7680
    imul eax, ebx   ; eax = 7680 * y (use imul form that does not set EDX)
    add eax, esi
    add eax, display_start
    mov [eax], ecx

    pop edi
    pop esi
    pop ebx
    ret

This preserves caller registers (except EAX) and conforms to the problem specification.
